usage: admin_cli.py [-h] [--api-url API_URL] [--region REGION]
                    {topics,findings,articles,feedback-config,inbox,approve,pipeline-config,review,lineage,stats,moderation,backup,failed-executions,security,sign-ins,musings,models,reviewer,model-catalog,model-config,model-rotation,refinements,equipment,prompts,evals} ...

BloggerBear admin operator CLI

positional arguments:
  {topics,findings,articles,feedback-config,inbox,approve,pipeline-config,review,lineage,stats,moderation,backup,failed-executions,security,sign-ins,musings,models,reviewer,model-catalog,model-config,model-rotation,refinements,equipment,prompts,evals}
    topics              Manage Topics
    findings            Research Findings
    articles            Manage articles
    feedback-config     When BloggerBear takes feedback: lockdown, rate limit, daily limit, per-
                        article limit
    inbox               What is waiting for you (articles, prompt changes, failed runs), at a
                        glance
    approve             Go through what is waiting for you, one keystroke each: y approve, r
                        reject, z skip, v read it all, q quit. Up to 30 at a time; run it again
                        for the next batch
    pipeline-config     Pipeline-wide settings (the default research interval, the draft review
                        mode, who may reach the assistant, the stagger between topics, the
                        dispatcher's shadow mode and start cap)
    review              How the fresh-data review of drafts is doing
    lineage             Audit and repair article lineage/cost data
    stats               Observability: one-time catch-up jobs
    moderation          Manage the moderation queue
    backup              Snapshot this deployment's content and configuration to one file, restore
                        one, or copy every article to another bucket
    failed-executions   View daily_cycle executions that exhausted their retries
    security            Security incidents: list them, move them along, or open one by hand
    sign-ins            Sign-ins to the operator's assistant: the log, and unlocking a user
    musings             The Musings feed: list the musings, fix one's text, or have one written
                        again
    models              Manage the AI model registry
    reviewer            Professor Grizzlewick, the reviewer bear: his tasks, limits and pause flag
                        (no deploy)
    model-catalog       The model discover and reprice jobs (every second day): pause flags,
                        sizes, reviews
    model-config        Manage the global default/fallback model
    model-rotation      The shared rotation pool: the models the daily cycle moves a topic's
                        model_id to
    refinements         Manage prompt refinements
    equipment           What the bear wears: armor (global guidance), rings (topic guidance), the
                        backpack
    prompts             Prompts as assets: what the publisher put in the prompts bucket, pausing
                        one version, the releases, and the kill switch
    evals               Continuous evals and the Model Ranch: settings, the rollup, status, a
                        digest, an operator's forgive, punish, gate override and revoked source,
                        and culling

options:

topics.help_text:
usage: admin_cli.py topics [-h] <action> ...

positional arguments:
  <action>
    list        List all topics
    get         Get one topic
    create      Create a topic
    update      Update a topic
    delete      Delete a topic
    trigger     Manually trigger a pipeline run
    candidates  List candidate ideas considered for a topic
    findings    Show the most recent research Finding for a topic
    schedule    Show every topic's slot, state, dispatch mode (its schedules or the queue) and the
                two schedules written for it, in plain words and as written (the stagger:
                docs/project-plan.md, Staggered schedules), and the dispatcher's shadow record
    reschedule  Rewrite every topic's two schedules with the stagger as it is now: after changing
                --stagger-minutes, after adding or deleting a topic (the daily delay is the number
                of topics), or to give older topics their slots. A topic on the queue has none
    pause       Pause a topic: no research tick, no candidate ideas, no daily article until it is
                resumed. Its schedules are disabled, the topic page says Paused, and the bear
                muses about it
    resume      Resume a paused topic: its schedules are enabled again from the next heartbeat

arguments.name: --adapter
arguments.help: Adapter key (default: web_search -- independent web research on the topic's name)

arguments.help: Topic-specific goal, e.g. '{"primary_focus": "...", "exclusion_criteria": "..."}'; omit to inherit the adapter/global default

arguments.name: --research-cadence
arguments.help: EventBridge Scheduler expression, e.g. 'rate(1 hour)' (default: rate(1 hour))

arguments.name: --research-interval-hours
arguments.help: Whole hours between real research runs (the --research-cadence schedule is only the heartbeat). Omit to inherit the pipeline-wide default

arguments.name: --findings-window-hours
arguments.help: How many hours back the daily article reads findings, never past the topic's last article: whole hours, 1 to 336 (default 24). Widen it for a topic that does not write every day (one day of a rotation, a weekly topic)

arguments.name: --review-mode
arguments.help: This topic's fresh-data review mode; omit to inherit the pipeline-wide mode

arguments.name: --daily-cadence
arguments.help: EventBridge Scheduler expression, e.g. 'cron(0 9 * * ? *)' (default: cron(0 9 * * ? *))

arguments.name: --daily-timezone
arguments.help: IANA zone the daily cron is read in (default: Australia/Sydney)

arguments.name: --stagger-slot
arguments.help: This topic's turn in the stagger: slot 1's research heartbeat runs at :05 past the hour, slot 2's at :10, ... (with the pipeline's stagger of 5 minutes), and its daily cycle the same way after every topic's heartbeat. Omit for the next free slot. `topics schedule` shows the result

arguments.name: --model-id
arguments.help: Pin this topic to one Bedrock model (overrides the global default); '' clears it

arguments.name: --fallback-model-id
arguments.help: Model to retry with if this topic's primary model call fails; '' clears it

arguments.name: --model-candidates
arguments.help: Comma-separated model IDs to rotate between -- one is picked at random per daily run, ahead of --model-id; '' clears rotation

arguments.help: network_prefetch (rail_access topics): fetch the topic's rail networks from Overpass with up to 90 s per reply, for a city too slow for the hourly tick; the next tick uses them. Never waits

arguments.name: --no-wait
arguments.help: Don't poll for completion after triggering -- just fire the request and return immediately (the old behavior). Default is to wait and report when the pipeline has actually finished, since the trigger itself is asynchronous.

articles.help_text:
usage: admin_cli.py articles [-h] <action> ...

positional arguments:
  <action>
    get              Show one article in any status: its title, topic, status, who published it,
                     what it cost, its sources and its full text. Nothing changes
    checked          Mark a financial article the reviewer bear approved as checked by you: clears
                     his flag, so he stops watching it for downvotes and the assistant stops
                     reporting it
    publish          Force-publish an article regardless of its current status
    unpublish        Take a published article down: delete its page, mark it rejected, remove its
                     musings and clear the CDN cache
    rewrite          Rewrite an article to fix what you say is wrong with it. A published article
                     stays up until its rewrite is ready, then comes down; the rewrite goes
                     through the reviews again and waits in the inbox
    feedback-lock    Stop taking feedback on one article (its feedback_locked flag, set to true)
    feedback-unlock  Take feedback on one article again (feedback_locked false). An article locked
                     because it reached its limit also needs --reset-count, or it stays at the
                     limit

arguments.name: --daily-timezone

arguments.name: --research-interval-hours

arguments.name: --review-mode
arguments.help: Fresh-data review of drafts: 'shadow' runs and records it without changing any outcome (the default), 'enforce' acts on it (revises minor problems, holds major ones), 'off' skips it; '' clears it (back to the default). A topic's own --review-mode overrides this

arguments.help: Who may reach the operator's assistant: 'open' any signed-in caller from anywhere (the default), 'allowlist' only from the operator's addresses, 'off' nobody; '' clears it (back to open). Applies from the next request, no deploy

arguments.name: --stagger-minutes
arguments.help: Minutes between one topic's schedules and the next (0-30): slot 1's research heartbeat at :05 past, slot 2's at :10, and every daily cycle one slot past the hour's last heartbeat, then one slot apart; 0 turns it off; '' clears it (back to 5). Then run `topics reschedule`

arguments.name: --dispatch-shadow
arguments.help: The dispatcher's shadow mode for topics still on their schedules: 'on' (the default) only records on each topic what it would have sent and counts mismatches against the schedules; 'off' leaves those topics alone. A topic on the queue is dispatched either way. '' clears it (back to on)

arguments.help: Daily cycles the dispatcher may start in one minute (1-10); the rest wait for the next minute. '' clears it (back to 3)

evals.help: Continuous evals and the Model Ranch: settings, the rollup, status, a digest, an operator's forgive, punish, gate override and revoked source, and culling
evals.help_text:
usage: admin_cli.py evals [-h]
                          {get,set,rollup,status,digest,forgive,punish,ungate,revoke,cull} ...

positional arguments:
  {get,set,rollup,status,digest,forgive,punish,ungate,revoke,cull}
    get                 Show the evals settings, the values in effect and the judge's model
    set                 Change evals settings (a setting not sent is unchanged; '' clears one);
                        the gates are edited in DynamoDB only
    rollup              Run the hourly rollup now: from its watermark, or for the days --from to
                        --to again
    status              Switches, the prompt release and the last 24 hours' prompt fallbacks, the
                        rollup, late events, the judge, gated models, the cull proposal and the
                        last cull applied, the eval-work and work.fifo queues and topics by
                        dispatch mode
    digest              Each model's and prompt version's day totals since a day (default: the
                        last 7 days)
    forgive             Raise a model's total by N, and no window, or record a forgive of a prompt
                        version (an Admin Forgive event): a model's total, which the total gate
                        and culling read, moves at the next hourly rollup; nothing adds up a
                        prompt version's adjustments yet
    punish              Lower a model's total by N, and no window, or record a punish of a prompt
                        version (an Admin Punish event): a model's total, which the total gate and
                        culling read, moves at the next hourly rollup; nothing adds up a prompt
                        version's adjustments yet
    ungate              Hold a model's gates open for some hours, whatever its scores
                        (ungated_until)
    revoke              Leave a source's events out of the rollup (added to excluded_sources); the
                        days already final that hold them are added up again, by a rollup it
                        starts or the `evals rollup` command it gives
    cull                Show the weekly cull proposal (models below the total gate that play no
                        role) and the last cull applied; --apply archives then deletes up to
                        cull_max_per_run of them, while culling is on

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
